presentation.label: SAMPLE LOCKS
presentation.summary: Lock Part sample choices into pattern trigs, or clear SAMPLE locks.
presentation.overview: Two explicit native SAMPLE-lock actions in Part Edit. The local emulator prototype stops playback before editing and defaults to retaining manual or unknown locks. Hardware and release qualification remain incomplete.
highlights: All eight tracks appear; only Flex and Static tracks are selectable.
Select all eligible tracks or a subset.
Keep existing sample locks by default.
Clear retains manual and unknown-origin locks by default.
usage: MKII: FUNC + PART, then choose either sample-lock action.
Level 2: arrows navigate eligible tracks; A selects all, B selects the highlighted track. Turn clockwise ON, counterclockwise OFF.
C sets Replace existing for Lock, or Retain manual locks for Clear.
YES opens level 3 with per-track change counts. NO returns to level 2; NO in level 2 closes.

limitations: Local emulator prototype only; physical power cycles, performance and full companion runtime behavior are not qualified.
Ownership material uses a tagged private battery-RAM region, bound to one project identity. It is not included when a project is copied to another instrument.

Same-value edits through the native SAMPLE editor retire ownership. Missing-module edit history, all reload/copy paths and removal/reinstall invalidation still need qualification; do not use on hardware yet.
Unknown or mismatched ownership is retained by default. Native card-build integration is not implemented.
Sparse battery store holds 704 active track/pattern combinations. A full store refuses new locking before any sample edit; it never evicts known ownership.

steps: FUNC + PART opens level 1; select an action with YES.
Level 2 always shows T1-4 left and T5-8 right. Arrows skip greyed-out non-Flex/Static tracks.
Turn A clockwise to select all eligible tracks or counterclockwise to clear selection. B sets the highlighted track in the same way.
Use C for the existing-lock policy. Clear retains manual locks by default.
YES opens level 3. Review per-track change counts; YES applies, NO returns to level 2.
NO in level 2 closes the popup. Apply stops playback first and leaves it stopped; a recorder in use refuses the edit.
